notes: Added the United Kingdom of the Netherlands (Congress of Vienna).
The Punjab was the Sikh Empire of Ranjit Singh, not Maratha.
Hong Kong became British only in 1841.
Restored the Dutch East Indies from the 1800 map.
Florida was Spanish until 1821.
The Río de la Plata had been self-governing since 1810.
Split 'Turan' into Khiva, Bukhara, Kokand and the Kazakh juzes.
Filled gaps in the source map from the nearest map (within 50 years).
Filled unclaimed land with peoples and cultures from neighbouring maps.
Named the remaining unclaimed regions after their regional peoples.
"Malaya" is a British-era name; the peninsula and its neighbours were Malay sultanates.
Somalia is a 20th-century state; the region was held by Somali sultanates and clans.
The Canary Islands were conquered by Castile by 1496; the Guanche territory is Castilian/Spanish here.
There was no Senegal before the French colony; the area was held by the Wolof and Fula kingdoms.
The Kingdom of Benin and the Niger delta were labelled "Sotho", a people of southern Africa; the land west of it was labelled "Africa".
Territories filed under the wrong realm are moved to their own (for example the islands of South-East Asia, Travancore and Cochin, Cochin China, Sardinia).
Two different states with one name are named apart (for example the Kingdom of Kongo and the modern Congo).
States drawn after they ended, or before they began, are replaced by what held the land on this map’s date.
The Maratha Confederacy is cut back to its own lands; Rajputana, the Punjab, Sindh and the other states around it are drawn as they were.
The Merina kingdom ruled central Madagascar until the French conquest of 1895-1897; the rest of the island was held by the Sakalava and other kingdoms.
The ancient kingdom of Hadramaut was annexed by Himyar about 300. The Kathiri Sultanate ruled the Hadramaut from 1395, and the Mahra Sultanate the coast to its east until 1967.
Small mapping specks were joined to their neighbours.
